The financial impact is expected to last weeks. The Microsoft outage is calculated to cost Australian businesses billions of dollars, with experts warning small businesses will be the hardest hit by the technology failure. A widespread outage, which started about 3:15 am AEDT, on Friday, has hit platforms including Outlook, with many users having trouble accessing emails and encountering errors across the Microsoft suite of products. Workers across multiple types of businesses have reported being unable to access email or SharePoint, with some resorting to using fax machines to keep operating. Microsoft outage live: For the latest on the issues affecting the tech giant's apps, read our blog. RSM Australia Risk Advisory partner Ashwin Pal said the cost to professional service businesses, such as lawyers or accountants, would be hundreds of thousands of dollars per hour. "It's not just the initial downtime, it's more actually about then the catch up effort because that costs money," he said. "Because now when things do normalise, you're going to have to spend money to actually catch up because of all the backlog." Ashwin Pal says Monday's backlog of work will be costly. ( Supplied ) He said the impact of the outage was amplified by the 3.9 million businesses globally that used the Microsoft suite, with many not having backup systems, resulting in huge costs to the economy. "This is what happened with CrowdStrike. So when the outage happened, because of where we are in the world in terms of time zones, we felt the impact first. "As the US and Europe come online, and they can't operate, it's going to get worse. So you're going to have a multiplier effect." Outlook down as Microsoft outage hits Australians Microsoft says it has begun restoring access to its email and other online services after Australians experienced outages for several hours today. He said the repercussions would be most keenly felt by small businesses, due to operating on thin margins. "You take a CBA as an example, they'll be able to absorb an impact like this a lot easier than the five-person accounting shop down the road," he said. "They were already actually working on very thin margins. All of a sudden they're actually out for three, four, five days or whatever it takes for them to recover. That could be the final straw." Owner of small Queensland business Regal Shower Screens, Tracey Tucker, said the lost day of business would cost at least $30,000, but there were numerous flow-on effects. "I'm paying my girls sitting in here in the office to do nothing," she said. "The phone rings, they can't order anything. "Then it puts undue pressure because if it's back online on Monday, everything we missed Friday, we're going to try to catch up on." Experts say the outage will hurt small business the most. ( Reuters: Dado Ruvic/Illustration ) She said the outage meant the business would struggle to meet its promoted deadlines because the glass manufacturers would also be inundated on Monday. "It's going to put pressure on everybody down the track because our girls are going to get yelled at, like, 'You just said my shower's going to be two weeks now, it's two and a half weeks', all because we can't send the order through today." Service delivery manager with telecommunication company Hubify, Chloe Mombeshora, said she had received numerous calls from less tech-savvy clients who were unsure what was happening. "They're thinking that their internet is down, they don't know what to do," she said. She added some clients had raised concerns the inability to communicate could impact their businesses' reputations. Some Outlook users were receiving notifications for emails they could not open. "We actually have to call each client individually, every single personal phone number, every single Teams number, hope it gets through and update them that way because the email service is just not working on their end either," he said. events.title: Outback cattle flown to Kazakhstan
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Hereford cattle from the middle of Australia flown to Kazakhstan Ben Hayes (second from right) alongside livestock agent Tim McKean, inspecting cattle with Kazakhstan buyers. ( Supplied: Undoolya Station ) A buyer from Kazakhstan has taken nearly 300 head of cattle from the Northern Territory after flying out to inspect them. Cattle producer Ben Hayes says Kazakhstan's government has an initiative to boost its national herd. Federal data shows Kazakhstan imported more than 1,000 head each of cattle and sheep in October. Nearly 300 head of cattle from a station near Alice Springs have been flown to Kazakhstan, in what local producers hope is the start of a new market. The distance from Alice Springs in the middle of Australia to Kazakhstan is roughly 10,000 kilometres. Ben Hayes from Undoolya Station said he got a call from his livestock agent one day with an interesting offer. "He asked if we had some heifers for this Kazakhstan job and we did," he said. "The buyer from Kazakhstan actually flew out here [with an interpreter], took a quick look and ended up taking them. "They got trucked down to Melbourne, where they stayed in quarantine for about a month and were then loaded into crates and onto the plane." Cattle from Undoolya Station ready for export to Kazakhstan. ( Supplied: Undoolya Station ) Mr Hayes said the animals were flown from Melbourne to Singapore and then onto Kazakhstan. "There was a weight limit on them of about 180 to 250 kilograms and they had to be preg-tested empty." He said the money paid for the animals was "on-par" with what he would normally receive in the Australian market. But he said the chance to be involved in the sale to Kazakhstan was "very special". "To know that our heifers are now becoming breeding stock for Kazakhstan is a feather in our cap, in Australia's cap," he said. ABC Landline has been told some cattle from Mt Riddock Station in the NT were also purchased for the consignment. According to data from the Federal Department of Agriculture, there were two flights of breeder cattle out of Victoria last month totalling 1,252 head. Another flight to Kazakhstan took 1,617 breeder sheep. It is understood Australia last exported cattle to Kazakhstan in 2019. It is a long way from Alice Springs to Kazakhstan. ( ABC Landline ) This is not the first time Undoolya Station has flown cattle to a distant market. In 1981, Undoolya steers were flown direct out of Alice Springs to Korea. "I was only a little fella at the time, but my father and grandfather flew steers out of Alice Springs on a Flying Tiger aircraft, straight to Korea" Mr Hayes said. "I don't know why they wanted steers, but that's what happened, Alice Springs is an international airport, it was a good opportunity." Undoolya Station is the Northern Territory's oldest pastoral lease. Established in 1872, the property has been owned by the Hayes family since 1906. events.title: Haze-linked First Resources, Bumitama post higher profits for Q3
events.summary: First Resources posted a 40.1% rise in its underlying net profit to US$122.7 million for the third quarter. First Resources posted a 40.1% rise in Q3 underlying net profit to US$122.7 million, helped by higher palm oil sales and stronger output after buying Austindo Nusantara Jaya. Bumitama’s Q3 net profit rose 1.9% to 614.1 billion rupiah, as better plantation and mill productivity lifted production, though dry weather hurt shipments. Both firms said biodiesel demand and higher energy prices may support palm oil, but they also stressed zero-burning policies and cooperation with authorities over the haze. SINGAPORE – Two palm oil companies linked to the transboundary haze in October reported higher profits for the third quarter ended Sept 30, in separate business updates published on the morning of Nov 13. Palm oil producer First Resources posted a 40.1% rise in its underlying net profit to US$122.7 million (S$157.9 million) for the third quarter of 2026, from US$87.5 million in the year-ago period. The increase was boosted by higher sales of palm oil products and fruit bunches harvested from oil palms, it said. Sales were up 24.9% at US$578.6 million for the quarter, compared with US$463.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation rose 26.6% to US$207.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, up from US$163.8 million a year ago. For the nine months ended Sept 30, sales grew 36.5% year on year to US$1.6 billion, driven by higher sales volumes. A net inventory drawdown of 28,000 tonnes over the nine-month period, compared with a build-up of 80,000 tonnes in the corresponding period in 2025, also supported higher sales volumes. The group’s stronger production output in the first nine months of 2026 was also attributable in part to the full nine-month contribution from Austindo Nusantara Jaya, an Indonesian agribusiness company acquired in May 2025. However, profits were partially offset by foreign currency translation losses resulting from the depreciation of the Indonesian rupiah against the US dollar. The group said it expects demand for palm oil to remain supported by Indonesia’s biodiesel programme. In addition, elevated crude oil prices arising from geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are expected to support biodiesel economics and crude palm oil demand. Performance supported by productivity improvements Meanwhile, Bumitama reported a 1.9% increase in its net profit to 614.1 billion rupiah (S$43.4 million) for the quarter ended Sept 30, compared with 602.9 billion rupiah in the previous corresponding period. For the nine-month period, net profit rose 30.6% to 2.4 trillion rupiah, up from 1.9 trillion rupiah in the year-ago period. Revenue increased 9.7% to 4.2 trillion rupiah in the third quarter, up from 3.9 trillion rupiah a year ago. For the nine-month period, revenue was up 20% at 16.3 trillion rupiah. Bumitama said its performance was supported by productivity improvements in its plantations and mills, particularly during the earlier part of the quarter. In July, internal production of fresh fruit bunches reached 383,203 tonnes, accounting for almost 40% of the quarter’s production. Quarterly production of crude palm oil increased 14% year on year to 368,323 tonnes. However, exceptionally dry weather conditions in its Kalimantan estates during the third quarter put additional pressure on logistics infrastructure and disrupted shipments, said Bumitama. Consequently, third-quarter revenue declined compared with the second quarter. The prolonged dry season also heightened the risk of land and forest fires across parts of Kalimantan. Fires affected certain areas within or adjoining the group’s concessions, including community-managed, conservation and unplanted land, the group noted. Bumitama said that elevated energy prices and Indonesia’s biodiesel programme coupled with a relatively constrained palm oil supply growth could provide a “supportive backdrop” for palm oil fundamentals heading into 2027. However, market conditions remain subject to uncertainty. These include changes in global energy prices, supply-and-demand dynamics, and the potential effects of prolonged dry weather on future production, it added. Both First Resources and Bumitama reiterated their commitment to upholding a zero-burning policy, and cooperating with the Indonesian and Singapore authorities in relation to the haze.

events.title: ST Engineering Q3 revenue rises 9% to $3.4 billion, declares interim dividend of 5 cents per share
events.summary: Defence and public security was the group’s largest revenue contributor for the nine-month period, generating some $4.3 billion. SINGAPORE – ST Engineering’s revenue for the third quarter ended September rose 9% year on year to $3.4 billion, from $3.1 billion in the previous corresponding period, the group said on Nov 13. The technology and engineering company declared a third-quarter interim dividend of five cents per share, up from four cents a year earlier. Its first-quarter and second-quarter dividends were four cents and five cents per share, respectively, bringing the total for the first three quarters to 14 cents per share. For the first nine months of 2026, revenue increased 10% to $10 billion, from $9.1 billion in the same period a year earlier. Excluding LeeBoy, its US-based construction equipment business divested on Sept 4, 2025, revenue grew 13% on a rebased basis. Defence and public security was the group’s largest revenue contributor for the nine-month period, generating some $4.3 billion, up 7% year on year. Excluding LeeBoy, revenue from the segment grew 13%. Third-quarter revenue rose 8% to $1.4 billion, or 12% on a rebased basis. The increase was led by marine and digital systems and cybersecurity businesses. The segment secured $5.5 billion in new contracts in the first nine months, including $1.8 billion in the third quarter . These included a five-year contract to supply 40mm ammunition to the British Ministry of Defence, projects involving defence command-and-control systems in Singapore, and maintenance and support services for the US Navy’s fleet. Meanwhile, commercial aerospace revenue rose 12% to about $4.1 billion in the first nine months, supported by higher contributions from engine maintenance, repair and overhaul work and nacelles, a container for aircraft parts. Revenue for the third quarter increased 7% to $1.4 billion. The segment secured $4.2 billion in new contracts in the first nine months, of which $1.4 billion was won in the third quarter . The latest wins included its first Airbus A220 airframe heavy maintenance contract with an Asia-Pacific operator and airframe maintenance agreements with Asia-Pacific airline customers. Revenue from urban solutions and satellite communications increased 15% year on year to about $1.7 billion in the first nine months. Third-quarte r revenue also rose 15% to $600 million, with higher contributions from both businesses. The segment secured $3.5 billion in new contracts in the nine-month period, including $2.4 billion in the third quarter . Wins included turnkey rail services for the Taoyuan MRT Brown Line and Green Line Extension in Taiwan, integrated smart security management solutions contracts in Singapore and tolling infrastructure modernisation work for the Tampa-Hillsborough Expressway Authority in the US. Across the group, contract wins totalled $13.2 billion in the first nine months, including $5.6 billion in the third quarter. The nine-month figure excluded $1.7 billion in New Jersey Turnpike Authority order book recognition. The group’s order book stood at a record $37.7 billion as at September, up from $33.2 billion as at end-2025. About $3.1 billion is expected to be delivered in the remainder of 2026. ST Engineering also reported a record-low operating expenses-to-revenue ratio of 9% for the first nine months, compared with 10.2% for the whole of 2025. The 2025 figure excluded a one-off impairment loss of iDirect group. Separately, ST Engineering said it is exploring long-term opportunities in the nuclear energy sector, drawing on its capabilities in complex, safe and mission-critical environments and partnering organisations with complementary expertise. Its current collaborations include those with the Agency for Science, Technology and Research, Sembcorp Utilities and Commonwealth Fusion Systems. Areas of activity include factory-fabricated structural modules, such as protective steel structures, and advanced materials for fusion reactors , including tungsten coatings for reactor’s inner walls . The group also sees opportunities to apply its capabilities in digital twin technology and artificial intelligence, advanced materials and manufacturing, and large-scale systems integration.

events.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
events.summary: How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security? Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December. Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X. "The American people deserve answers," he added. Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily on 3 December, but also warned the panel could issue a subpoena to compel his testimony. Three House of Representatives committees - on intelligence and foreign affairs and a panel on China - have also sent a letter to Huang summoning him for a closed-door interview on 1 December. How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House Published 1 day ago How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions Published 1 day ago Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently? Published 1 day ago The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal Published 1 day ago Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said. Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public. Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared. Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information. The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO.

events.title: Outlook email outage: Microsoft says service recovery completed in parts of Asia-Pacific
events.summary: Microsoft said on Friday its email services were being restored in parts of the Asia Pacific region, as it extended its email timeout to 48 hours to resolve an outage that affected systems globally on Thursday. The disruption affected Outlook, Teams and the Copilot AI service for millions of people, companies and governments around the world on Thursday, and the issue continued into Friday. "We've made additional progress towards service recovery, with recovery actions completed across portions of the affected infrastructure in the Asia Pacific region," the company said in its most recent update on Friday. "Traffic is being gradually restored and we're seeing improvements in key customer scenarios, including mailbox access and delayed email processing. However, some users may continue to experience intermittent issues." Reducing email queues and backlogs "remains a priority, and the extended 48-hour email timeout window remains in place to help protect delayed messages as delivery catches up", it added. The focus is now on extending the recovery actions across affected infrastructure in other regions. "At this time, we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident," the company added. "We will continue to treat this with urgency until full mitigation, and we will share a full post-incident report with root cause and defence-in-depth actions after mitigation is complete." The company delayed its email timeout window to 48 hours to help protect and keep delayed messages, such as emails sent from other providers, from being bounced back. After hours of troubleshooting, the company said its investigation indicated that failed checks "may originate from a specific component that's responsible for processing server health". "We've taken steps to prevent additional servers from being impacted while we work to return the affected servers to service", it said. “We're implementing these actions more broadly across affected regions as we seek to attain persistent recovery. ” The company said it was working to recover its front-end servers. To improve server stability and traffic, Microsoft previously said it was “adjusting traffic protocols, redistributing traffic and applying strategic traffic blocking measures”. Microsoft's outage reports on November 12 were recorded in 74 countries and territories in about an hour on Downdetector, an online service that monitors internet disruption. Microsoft said its Exchange Online incident began at 4.17pm in the US (8.17pm UAE time) on Thursday. In two hours, reports on five Microsoft services reached 19,650 a minute, compared with fewer than 15 a minute on an average Thursday, Downdetector said. Outlook reports peaked at more than 2,000 times their normal level. “Reports about Microsoft 365, Copilot, Teams and OneDrive each rose more than a hundred-fold, and Azure about 100-fold. Xbox, GitHub and LinkedIn, also Microsoft's, rose far less,” DownDetector said. Microsoft's outage reports on November 12 reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour on Downdetector. Microsoft says its Exchange Online incident began at 16:17 UTC. Reports to Downdetector about Outlook began climbing at about 17:25 UTC, 12:25 in New York. By 18:25,… pic.twitter.com/7FQ4dDsfbm — Downdetector (@downdetector) November 12, 2026 The outage "highlights the need for resilience in all our critical systems", said Jack Hidary, chief executive at tech company SandboxAQ. "The energy grid, the telco network and the applications layers are all now essential to business continuity. Often these outages occur not from cyber attacks, but from code updates within the system that has unforeseen consequences. "Code simulation [CodeSim] is emerging as a new field that can detect potential impact of code updates before they are committed to production. CodeSim will prevent many of these outages in the future," he added. Microsoft's status website first acknowledged the problem on Thursday. “Users may be unable to connect to their mailboxes in Exchange Online through multiple connection methods,” a message on the Microsoft page said. Over the course of the day, the company added to its tally of products that users might not be able to access. Services for technologists, including cyber security software, file-sharing services and administrator tools, were also disrupted. We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. — Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 12, 2026 For Outlook specifically, Microsoft classified the issue as being a “service degradation”. A social media post from Microsoft explained efforts to rectify the problem. “We've begun redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load,” it said. Later on Thursday, data from Downdetector indicated that services started to recover for some users. For many, however, problems continued for several hours. Microsoft later confirmed through its service health status update page that the technical issue broadly affected the company's Microsoft 365 productivity suite. The technology company also said it was able to gain more insights into the cause of the problem experienced by so many users around the world. “We determined the elevated load isn't driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable,” the update said. Governments and various companies around the world were also affected by the problem. As a result, many sought to calm the frustrations felt by patrons and customers through social media posts. “Due to a wide-scale outage impacting Microsoft 365 across North America, the State of Michigan is currently experiencing technical issues with email and other Microsoft applications,” Michigan's Department of Technology, Management and Budget said in a post. “Responses to emails may be delayed during this time.” Later on Thursday evening, Microsoft said it was still looking at “all available pathways to restore service”, but that those efforts “have not provided the anticipated relief”. The company indicated that it was pursuing a different strategy of “re-isolating a portion of infrastructure” and also restarting certain components that it speculated were causing the problem. More than seven hours after the problem was first reported, Microsoft warned that certain servers that were returned to service might become unresponsive once traffic started moving through them.

events.title: Singapore says US authorities, and Supermicro, hardly helped investigation of Jensen Huang’s Chinese friend
events.summary: The government of Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs has revealed it investigated Alice Huang, the woman who is an alleged Chinese intelligence asset and had an intimate relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and a possible entanglement with troubled server-maker Supermicro. US authorities provided only “limited assistance” in the matter, despite Singapore asking for help. The Ministry outlined its activities in a statement published late on Thursday, Singapore time. The document reveals that Singapore’s Police Force (SPF) and Customs agency commenced an investigation into Ms. Huang’s company, Megaspeed, in February 2025. “The suspected domestic offences pertained to potential false declarations in relation to the purchase of servers and other related offences,” the Ministry wrote, adding that the exec “was not investigated for espionage.” Singaporean authorities wanted to know if servers bought by local companies, but exported to Malaysia without ever touching Singaporean soil, might have ended up in a third country. It is not unusual for Singapore-based companies to acquire goods that never reach the island, because it promotes itself as the ideal spot from which to run an operation that trades across Asia. Singapore does so because it is tiny – the whole nation is the same size as the five boroughs of New York City. That small size means Singapore restricts the number of datacenters that can operate on its soil. Those limits are a big reason why Malaysia’s Johor region, which is under 20kms from the border with Singapore and a joint special economic zone, has become a major datacenter province. Singapore needs deals like that to thrive but works hard to ensure its hospitality is not abused. Which is why it felt Megaspeed’s activities worthy of investigation. US authorities were interested too. On 24 June 2025, the Bureau of Industry and Security, which regulates sensitive goods subject to export controls, visited Megaspeed in Singapore to check the hardware it bought arrived at its intended destination. Ms. Huang attended that event and later met the SPF for an interview. That meeting ended with the SPF impounding her passport, so it could keep her in Singapore while the investigation continued. As the matter progressed, the SPF suspected perennially troubled server-maker Supermicro had a role in this situation. Readers may recall that the US Department of Justice indicted two Supermicro execs for conspiring to ship servers to China in contravention of US law. Supermicro investigated the matter and parted ways with three staff who acted improperly. The company has denied ever selling to Megaspeed. Singaporean authorities say they received only “limited cooperation” from Supermicro, so in July 2025 the office of the nation’s Attorney General asked US authorities for help. “Since September 2025, SPF has repeated this request on several occasions to the US Department of Justice and the Federal Bureau of Investigation,” the statement reveals. “Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company.” In February 2026, the SPF “concluded that there was insufficient evidence to establish that Huang had committed any offences relating to the possible inaccurate declarations for which Megaspeed was being investigated.” But the police did decide that Ms. Huang provided inaccurate information “to downplay her role in Megaspeed.” “She was issued a stern warning and barred from re-entering the country.” The police returned her passport and Ms. Huang left Singapore on the same day. The Singaporean statement shows the island nation wants the world to know it does not facilitate sanction-busting activity and takes even the hint of it seriously. That matters to Nvidia, too, because Singaporean buyers sometimes account for over 20 percent of its quarterly revenue and may continue to do so. Whoever replaces Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO will surely face many questions about the company’s practices. Singapore may just have made answering those queries a little easier. ®

events.title: Mount Isa's $145 million critical minerals pitch one step closer
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Mount Isa critical minerals hub gets early government backing Federal and state governments have agreed to fund a feasibility study into a new research facility in Mount Isa. ( ABC News: Harriet Tatham ) A business case for a $145 million critical mineral research hub in Mount Isa has secured funding for a feasibility study. The centre will provide early analysis and testing for prospective mines trying to scale operations in the region. The federal and state governments have agreed to tip in $241,250 each to fund trials, with an additional $482,500 to come from Mount Isa City Council. Mount Isa's push to reinvent its regional economy with a new mineral research hub has secured state and federal backing for a feasibility study. Mount Isa City Council and the University of Queensland released a business case earlier this month for a $145 million critical minerals research centre. The facility would allow mining companies to analyse rock samples from local mineral deposits to see what minerals were present and if they would be viable to mine. The $145 million centre is expected to create up to 50 permanent jobs. ( Supplied: Mount Isa City Council ) In July 2025, Mount Isa's underground copper mine closure saw nearly 500 workers sacked in the 19,000-strong community, forcing the council to search for economic alternatives. While Mount Isa's economy has been affected, exploration and investment across the wider North West Minerals Province has boomed, with about 85 critical minerals projects underway. Sustainable Minerals Institute director at the University of Queensland Rick Valenta said the proposed hub would allow industry to scale operations quickly. Rick Valenta (right) says the facility will help mines understand what minerals are in deposits and how they could be mined. ( ABC Rural: Eric Barker ) "The reason you can't just find a deposit and put it into production in a year is because you've got to answer … 'What's the content of the metal that you're after? And … how do we get the metals out of that rock?'" Professor Valenta said. "[At the moment], those rocks would be going elsewhere in Queensland … Australia or the world … [and] that involves a cost and a delay. "This centre is aimed at providing a local solution to that sort of thing." The proposed research centre would be situated between the George Fisher Mine and Mount Isa Airport. ( Supplied: Mount Isa City Councill ) Mount Isa Mayor Peta MacRae said she hoped the research hub would help future-proof the city by giving mining companies a dedicated site to research problems locally. "[Currently] minerals are just going to be ripped up and shipped," she said. "What we want to do is add the value and do as much processing as we can … to help us secure the future for our communities." Peta MacRae hopes the project will centralise some of the regions' mining investment into the town's economy. ( ABC News: Abbey Halter ) The proposed hub is expected to create up to 50 permanent jobs and would be located near the Mount Isa Airport. On Friday morning, Federal Assistant Minister for Resources Anthony Chisholm confirmed funding would be released to consider the proposal. "We want to make the most of these opportunities … and ensure that Mount Isa remains a great place to live and work and attract people at the same time," he said. "We know that there is enormous potential, but it's about proving that and then also ensuring that we can attract the industry investment." Anthony Chisholm says the cenrre is about proving Mt Isa's potential and attracting industry investment. ( ABC News: Tim Little ) The federal and state governments have agreed to tip in $241,250 each to fund a feasibility study, with an additional $482,500 to come from Mount Isa City Council. If successful, the hub would operate in conjunction with similar facilities in Mackay and Townsville. Initial testing and analysis would start at Mount Isa's centre, before small-scale piloting took place in Mackay followed by large-scale trials in Townsville. events.title: Chris Van Hollen to challenge Schumer for Senate majority leader
events.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen announced Thursday that he'll challenge Chuck Schumer for majority leader. Why it matters: Van Hollen's bid gives grassroots activists nearly three weeks to pressure Senate Democrats before they cast secret ballots in the Dec. 1 leadership election. The attempt to oust Schumer (D-N.Y.) underscores that deep divisions are plaguing the Democratic Party despite its overwhelming midterm success . Van Hollen (D-Md.) has served in the Senate since 2017 and has been in Congress since 2003. Schumer has been the Senate Democratic leader since 2017 and has served in the Senate since 1999. Driving the news: "In this election, the American people called for change," Van Hollen said in a statement on Thursday. "They called for a change from Donald Trump's disastrous policies — but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn't working for working people." "It's now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership. This is not about any one person — it's about answering the call of the American people. That is why I'm running for Senate Majority Leader." In a statement of his own, Schumer said: "I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic leader." Zoom in: Van Hollen acknowledged he's the "underdog" in the race but claimed Thursday on MS NOW he has "more than 10" senators on his side. "[T]he time is now for change," Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) said Tuesday. He appeared with Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), who demanded a plan for change from party leadership. Progressives have accused Schumer of not fighting hard enough against President Trump and the MAGA agenda. At least six senator-elects, including Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.), Adam Hamilton (Kansas), Julia Stratton (Ill.), Peggy Flanagan (Minn.), Troy Jackson (Maine) and Annie Andrews (S.C.) have said they won't support Schumer for leader. El-Sayed immediately endorsed Van Hollen upon his entry in the race. The other side: Schumer has more public backers at this stage than Van Hollen. That includes Sen. Angus King (I-Maine), Sen.-elect Sherrod Brown (Ohio) and Democratic Sens. John Fetterman (Pa.), Ruben Gallego (Ariz.), Kirsten Gillibrand (N.Y.), Mark Kelly (Ariz.), Jacky Rosen (Nev.), Brian Schatz (Hawaii) and Sheldon Whitehouse (Rhode Island). Editor's note: This is a breaking news story and has been updated.

events.title: US firm Advent seeks to sell Singapore tutor chain Learning Lab again, sources say
events.summary: Advent invested in The Learning Lab in 2014, but there has been no publicly available information on how much stake it holds. Advent International is trying to sell Singapore tutor chain The Learning Lab again, its second attempt since 2021, sources say, with a planned price of US$400 million to US$500 million. Some sale proceeds will repay a S$265 million private credit facility from KKR, HPS Investment Partners and Nomura, which matures in 2027. The deal comes as private education investment in Asia fell 87% to US$240 million in 2025, with AI worries and many firms still trying to exit investments. SINGAPORE – US buyout firm Advent International has put up Singapore’s tutor-chain The Learning Lab for sale, marking its second attempt since 2021 to unload the asset, in part to repay debt, according to people familiar with the matter. Advent has hired an adviser to kick-start the sale process and plans to offer the company for about US$400 million to US$500 million (S$514.6 million to S$643.3 million), said the people who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private. Some of the proceeds will be used to settle a S$265 million private credit facility jointly provided by KKR & Co, HPS Investment Partners and Nomura Holdings in 2023 and which will mature in 2027 , they said. Representatives for Advent, KKR and Nomura declined to comment. HPS did not respond to a request for comment. Private money has been pouring into schools in Asia in recent years as investors seek to profit from growing demand for quality education. Financiers such as Apollo Global Management and KKR have bought stakes and lent to school chains, hoping that a growing number of rich people in the region would fuel expansion. But private equity and venture capital investment in education services in Asia slumped 87% to US$240 million in 2025 , according to S&P Global, citing more rigorous deal selection and the potential impact of artificial intelligence on the sector. Another key challenge is the backlog of private equity firms seeking to exit companies they have bought into. Advent invested in The Learning Lab in 2014, but there has been no publicly available information on how much stake it holds. People with knowledge of the matter said Advent fully owns the learning company. The Learning Lab provides education for pre-school, primary, secondary and junior college students in Singapore, according to its website. It also has online services for other Asian markets including Malaysia, Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia. In Singapore, the company charges about S$702 a month for its junior college programmes. events.title: ATSB releases preliminary report into young pilot's NT crash
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts ATSB releases preliminary report into Bob Bramley's NT plane crash Bob Bramley was flying to pick up passengers for a return trip when his plane crashed. ( Supplied ) The Australian Transport Safety Bureau has released its preliminary report on the August crash of pilot Bob Bramley. Bramley is believed to have died when his plane dived into the water off Groote Eylandt, in the Northern Territory. Fishermen witnessed young Tasmanian pilot Bob Bramley's plane crash in waters off the Northern Territory in August "at very high speed", a report has revealed. The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) today released its preliminary report into the crash in the Gulf of Carpentaria on August 25 this year, which is believed to have killed 23-year-old Bramley. Northern Territory Police conducted extensive marine and air searches at the time, which recovered parts of the plane, but Bramley has never been found. At the time, 23-year-old Bob Bramley was working as a charter company pilot. ( Supplied. ) As a teenager, he became a passionate advocate for suicide prevention, and sought to raise awareness by becoming the youngest person to circumnavigate Australia solo by plane. Friends and family expressed their shock and sadness in the wake of the crash, remembering Bramley as a "beacon of hope", and for his love of flying. The ATSB report detailed the circumstances of the August crash, but noted the investigation is continuing and that a final report will be published at its conclusion. Fishers found plane parts in sea after crash The report, which refers to "the pilot" but does not identify Bramley, details his movements on the morning of August 25, as he prepared to fly between the small communities of Gove and Numbulwar in the Northern Territory. At the time, Bramley had been working as a pilot for aviation operator Air Frontier for more than a year, and had been the company's senior base pilot for the Arnhem region since April. The report noted that after fuelling the plane and lodging a flight plan, the Beechcraft 58 Baron plane departed from the Gove Airport at about 11am, with only the pilot on board. "The flight plan for the return to Gove indicated four passengers were to be on board," the report noted. The ATSB's map of Bob Bramley's final flight on August 25, 2026. ( ATSB/Google Earth ) About half an hour later, at 11:27am, fishermen in a boat south-west of Isle Woodah in the west of the Gulf of Carpentaria watched the plane pass overhead. "They expected the aircraft to pull up; however, it did not change trajectory, and it impacted the water at very high speed. "The witnesses motored to the impact point and found a fuel/oil slick on the water surface along with many small floating fragments of shattered airframe." NT Police image of wreckage underwater at the crash site. ( NT Police ) No audio recording of cockpit before crash The report noted that the Baron was not fitted with, and was not required to have, a flight data recorder or a cockpit voice recorder. The ATSB said the flight wasn't detected by radar, and data tracking the flight was recorded by Bramley's iPad, which it was transmitting to the online platform OzRunways. The final data point was transmitted at 11:24am, about 23 kilometres north of the crash site. Bramley made two radio broadcasts during taxi and take-off, and phone records indicated "maintained a messaging stream with their partner" throughout the flight. The report noted Bramley's qualifications to operate the Baron aircraft, that he held a valid medical certificate and that he had completed a multi-engine instrument proficiency check the previous month. Bramley had more than 1,138 hours total flight time, more than 300 of which were in the Baron. The Baron itself was initially built in 1978 and had been serviced most recently in June in Darwin. The report noted no significant weather activity was observed on the day, consistent with the witnesses and other pilots flying in the area. The report noted Bramley made two radio broadcasts during taxi and takeoff, and "maintained a messaging stream with their partner" throughout the flight. ( Supplied: Lachlan Bennett ) Large parts of plane, including engine, found in sea floor In August, NT Police Acting Assistant Commissioner Peter Malley said the search for Bramley and the crash site had been particularly difficult, adding that "tiger sharks and crocs" had complicated efforts. NT Police confirmed today that human remains had not been found. Police divers had to contend with sharks and crocodiles during search efforts.

events.title: Stocks recover from Nvidia whiplash, dollar climbs with US yields
events.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Nov 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. Stocks in Asia steadied after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned over affair claims, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, shaking the AI sector and chip supply chain. Investors lifted US Treasury yields and the dollar as they priced in a bigger Fed rate hike in December, while the yen stayed near 160 per dollar and risked intervention. Markets also tracked wider fallout from the AI slump, with Nvidia shares and related stocks falling, while rivals may gain and senators sought testimony on the company’s recent troubles. SINGAPORE – Stocks in Asia were on steadier footing on Nov 13 after a turbulent week dominated by revelations of extramarital affairs involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang that culminated in his resignation, in a blow to the global AI boom he helped advance. US Treasury yields climbed, with the two-year yield hitting a one-month high, lifting the dollar as investors weighed the prospect of an outsized 50 basis point rate hike by the US Federal Reserve in December. Huang stepped down on Nov 12 after reports of the affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, which plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves through the AI industry. His exit could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader artificial intelligence industry and supply chain, given Huang’s push to preserve access to the Chinese market as well as his close ties with US President Donald Trump. “His departure leaves a vacuum that will be difficult to fill... We do not assume existing commitments change, but new deals could take longer or require more compensation as investors look for reassurance about Nvidia’s role,” analysts at JPMorgan said in a note. “The bigger implications are for the rest of the AI trade, particularly GPU (graphics processing unit) financing and infrastructure deals in which Nvidia would presumably be involved as a supplier, investor or provider of contractual support.” Nvidia shares fell 3% in extended trading, while those of its customers, including South Korea’s Naver, extended declines on Nov 13 , with Naver down 2.75%. Jon Zauderer, Citi’s head of specialist sales, said competitors such as AMD, Arista and Broadcom could benefit from the Nvidia fallout. “If you think about the uncertainty that’s created about a potential management change, investors are going to look for alternatives,” he said. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 0.26%, reversing some of its 1.3% fall from the previous session. South Korea’s Kospi rose 2.35%, while Japan’s Nikkei added 1.4%. The recovery in global equities also follows last week’s market meltdown sparked by US Republicans’ electoral drubbing, which stoked fears that tighter regulation could slow the AI infrastructure build-out that has helped send stocks to record highs in 2026 . Nasdaq futures and S&P 500 futures rose more than 0.2% each, while EURO STOXX 50 futures fell 0.37%. US Senate Banking Committee chairman Tim Scott sent letters on Nov 12 to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Huang, asking them to testify over the recent developments at Nvidia. Concerns over the AI outlook also spilt into metals, with London copper prices hitting a four-month low in the previous session on fears of weaker demand, while shares of Australian-listed miner Capstone Copper Corp fell more than 5% on Nov 13 . The two-year US Treasury yield peaked at 4.8920% in the early Asian session, while the benchmark 10-year yield rose to a three-week high of 5.1433%. Investors now see a 14.5% chance of a jumbo 50-basis-point Fed hike in December, up from zero a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool. “Right now, the US Fed has three hikes priced in for effectively the next 12 months... The (most recent) CPI (consumer price index) print obviously was a bit hotter than expected. If those kinds of prints continue to happen, we can definitely see the Fed hiking three more times. It’s very within the realms of possibility,” said Manusha Samaraweera, fixed income investment director at Capital Group. The increasingly hawkish Fed expectations in turn boosted the dollar, which was on track for a weekly gain of 0.9%, its biggest in more than a month. The strength in the greenback, meanwhile, weighed on the yen, which languished close to the key 160 per dollar level on Nov 13 , leaving traders on alert for any intervention from Tokyo. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York said on Nov 12 it bought 79.4 billion yen (S$638.9 million) in the spot market on July 31, selling euros from the Exchange Stabilization Fund as part of a joint US-Japan intervention this summer to shore up the yen.

events.title: Genting Singapore shares fall as high rollers play less, resort revamp continues
events.summary: Net profit fell 42% year on year to $54.7 million for the three months ended Sept 30, while revenue fell 13% to $566.1 million. Genting Singapore’s profit fell 42% to S$54.7 million and revenue dropped 13% to S$566.1 million, as high rollers played less at Resorts World Sentosa. Casino revenue fell 22% to S$315 million, hit by weaker premium gambling and a lower share of wagers kept in September, though Genting said this matched regional trends. RWS is still being upgraded through 2027, with marketing, events and new Weave openings aimed at drawing premium visitors and boosting long-term appeal. SINGAPORE – Shares of Genting Singapore were down by more than 6% at 57 cents at noon on Nov 13, after the company reported another quarter of shrinking profits, as high rollers played less at Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) and ongoing renovations at the resort crimped visitor footfall and spending. Net profit fell 42% year on year to $54.7 million for the three months ended Sept 30, while revenue fell 13% to $566.1 million, Genting Singapore said in a business update on Nov 12. Both net profit and revenue for the July to September quarter were also lower than in the previous quarter from April to June. Casino revenue fell 22% to $315 million for the quarter under review compared with a year ago, as lower activity among premium gamblers and a lower-than-usual share of wagers retained by the casino in September further dented revenue. However, Genting said this was in line with trends in key regional markets. The group said adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation for the quarter, a measure of operating performance, would have been about $36 million higher than the reported $161.8 million if the casino had kept its usual share of premium wagers. Outside the casino, non-gaming revenue rose 1% year on year to $250.9 million for the quarter, despite fewer hotel rooms being available. This was up 29% from the previous quarter, although Genting did not elaborate on what drove the increase. The resort operator is banking on the year-end holiday season to draw visitors, even as upgrades to its hotels, gaming areas and other guest spaces limit how much of the resort it can operate through 2027. As part of efforts to attract premium customers, the resort is stepping up its marketing and using events and new openings at Weave, its retail and dining precinct, to give guests more reasons to visit. At the same time, RWS is revamping its gaming areas, lounges, restaurants and other guest spaces. It expects the upgrades to improve its hotel offerings and broaden the resort’s appeal over the longer term.

events.title: No love for Lambo: Luxury car dealer EuroSports reports losses, seeks funding to support business
events.summary: Lamborghini is expected to introduce a new version of its Temerario sports car (pictured on April 22) by March 2027. EuroSports Global’s losses widened as car sales fell, with revenue down more than 30% to $7.83 million. It blamed weak demand, high luxury car fees and economic uncertainty. The dealer hopes new Lamborghini models, including the Urus SE, will lift orders. It also expects the Temerario to arrive by March 2027. Its Scorpio Electric unit has won European and Singapore approval for the Lambda Scorpii motorcycle. EuroSports is seeking funding, as losses and short-term debts raise concern over its ability to keep operating. SINGAPORE – Singapore’s Lamborghini dealer EuroSports Global is looking to new luxury models to draw buyers after a tough quarter of falling sales, even as it seeks fresh funding to support its car business and plans to mass-produce a home-grown electric motorcycle. The group on Nov 12 said its net loss had widened to $1.24 million in the quarter ended Sept 30, from $752,000 a year earlier. Revenue fell by more than 30% to $7.83 million. For the first half of its financial year, the group’s net loss widened by 57% to $2.29 million as revenue fell 21.7% to $15.1 million, weighed down by falling car sales and thinner margins on cars sold. EuroSports is the distributor for Lamborghini and Touring Superleggera in Singapore, with some models selling for more than $2 million. However, hefty additional registration fees for luxury vehicles and rising certificate of entitlement premiums have crimped demand for high-end supercars here. EuroSports also expects economic and geopolitical uncertainty to make buyers more cautious in the months ahead. But the group said new models could help attract more orders, and expects to start delivering two new versions of Lamborghini’s Urus SE sport utility vehicle in the October-to-December quarter, although prices for this model may be lower. Lamborghini is also expected to introduce a new version of its Temerario sports car by March 2027 , following the recent launch of its Revuelto SV . EuroSports’ electric motorcycle business has a longer timeline. The Lambda Scorpii, developed by its subsidiary Scorpio Electric, became the first electric motorcycle designed from scratch in Singapore to secure European vehicle-type approval in 2025, the group said. The approval certifies that the motorcycle meets European Union safety, environmental and technical standards. The motorcycle secured approval from Singapore’s Land Transport Authority on June 12, and Scorpio Electric registered the first unit for use on Singapore roads on July 13. It is also setting up sales and servicing networks in the Asia-Pacific and Europe, with plans to build a network of distributors and dealers across 10 to 15 cities. EuroSports expects mass production and deliveries to begin in 2028, and is in the process of securing additional funding to support the commercialisation of this business. The company has spent heavily on research and development for the Lambda Scorpii , which has placed pressure on its financials over the years. The group disclosed in its financial statements that its losses, cash outflow and short-term obligations raised a material uncertainty over its ability to continue operating. In the first half, it burned through $1.18 million in cash to run its operations. As at Sept 30, what it owed in the short term exceeded its short-term assets – which included cash, cars and spare parts held for sale, and money that customers owe the company – by $6.54 million. Still, the board said it expects the car distribution business to generate enough cash to cover operating expenses over the next 12 months. It is in talks with financial institutions and potential investors for additional funding to support operations over at least that period.

events.title: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 re-educated with a more Western worldview
events.summary: An American AI lab has re-educated Qwen3.8-27B, a popular open-weight large language model from Alibaba, so the software forgets its Chinese ancestry. Nous Research, an Austin, Texas-based AI lab, has subjected the model to re-education through training, not to be confused with China's " Re-education Through Labor " system. With the help of a post-training process, Qwen3.8-27B has been reborn under the name Arete "to reinforce Western values on a Chinese-trained model." What qualifies as a "Western value" remains open to interpretation. "Open-weight Chinese models are among the strongest available, but they ship with state-aligned behavior baked into the weights," Nous Research wrote in a blog post . Your correspondent tested this with a variant model, Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-6bit, locally. Asked about events during 1989 in Tiananmen Square, the model either refused to discuss the topic or provided euphemistic response. What's perhaps more surprising is that Anthropic claims operators affiliated with Alibaba's Qwen lab used outputs from its Claude models to train competing AI models via distillation . Nous Research, maker of the Hermes Agent , cites that sort of censorship as a risk for users of AI models trained in China. The concern comes amid broader scrutiny of Chinese influence in the tech industry, heightened by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation following controversy involving a woman US intelligence has accused of spying for China. Nous says the risk posed by Chinese-made AI models go beyond promoting Beijing's worldview. Some Middle Kingdom models have been found to produce more vulnerable code under certain conditions, according to a study by Booz Allen Hamilton, which does a lot of business with the US government. Hirundo, a vendor which says it is building "the first Machine Unlearning Platform to ensure that AI models only know what they should," makes the same argument . The company also notes that its efforts to apply "unlearning" to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B saw a dramatic drop in output that reflects Communist Party of China's preferred censorship, propaganda messaging, or bias. 89.8 percent of the model's output reflected those values before unlearning reduced the incidence to 2.8 percent. Nous Research did not achieve such dramatic results, but did see an overall reduction in viewpoints deemed to be propaganda. "On our evaluation, Arete-27B raised its fact score from 2.32 to 2.98 out of 5 and cut answers containing propaganda from 22 percent to 1 percent, in line with the Western models we tested," the company said. To handle Arete's unlearning, Nous Research says it briefly considered Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Ultra , "but had found evidence that it too had a checkered record on China-related topics." "We don't know definitively, but theorize that the bias imparted to Nemotron came from working with Chinese open models during the training process," the company said. "We have experienced similar contamination, because the vast majority of high quality open models are Chinese, and only open models have terms of use that permit this kind of tinkering and experimentation." In the end, the biz tapped Inkling , an open weight model from US-based Thinking Machines Lab, to act as the teaching model. Nous Research says its model re-education efforts show that the propaganda layer is shallow and, with 50 million tokens worth of supervised learning, is relatively easy to remove. ®

events.title: Burnham says 'win-win' deal can be agreed between UK and EU
events.summary: Andy Burnham said he believes a "win-win" deal can be agreed with the European Union, adding it could be "more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for" in 2016. The prime minister is exploring closer ties with the bloc and is expected to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility at a UK-EU summit on 20 November. Speaking after meeting European leaders in Ireland on Thursday, Burnham said he hopes a deal could help lower prices and boost the UK economy. He predicted the negotiations could "go down to the wire". The Conservatives have previously said Labour are "dragging us into the European Union via the back door with their EU reset". While Burnham has argued that Brexit has done "more harm than good", he has ruled out major changes to the UK's relationship with the EU before the next general election. Labour's 2024 general election manifesto pledged there would be "no return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement", and Burnham has committed to this. The manifesto also said the party wanted to "make Brexit work" and reset the UK's relationship with the EU. Former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer struck a deal in May 2025 covering fishing, trade and other areas and next week's summit will see the UK government seek to agree further changes. Burnham has also made clear he wants to examine the "pros and cons" of the options for Britain's long-term relationship with the bloc. Burnham's push for closer EU ties causes ripples in his party and others Published 2 days ago UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC Published 6 days ago Brexit referendum 'possible' in Labour election manifesto, says Burnham Published 30 September Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion? Published 1 day ago Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Burnham was asked to explain if his decision to reopen the debate on the UK's future with Europe had helped or hindered the negotiations linked to the summit. Burnham replied "I think it has helped" before adding: "We've got a big week ahead of us to try and get this deal over the line. "But let's be clear what's at stake: what we can achieve through this deal is lower prices for British consumers, lower costs for British businesses, more growth in our economy so there's really big prizes here, and I will fight now over the days to come to make sure we get this deal over the line." Pressed on whether discounted university tuition fees for European students would be part of the deal, Burnham said "requests are coming from the European side, we are putting our requests on the table too". He added: "I believe there is a good deal to be done that could be a win-win for Britain and Europe. I think it actually could be more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for in 2016." Ahead of the summit, the UK and EU agreed a draft deal on removing post-Brexit checks from food and agriculture exports. Similar texts for deals on emissions trading and a youth travel and work scheme have also been circulated to EU nations. As a result of the agreement, the government claims the UK economy will eventually see £5.1bn worth of annual benefits. Burnham also told MPs last month that the summit presents an opportunity to make progress on "controlling illegal immigration". Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has previously strongly opposed any move to align with EU rules, saying it would "actually take us backwards". On Thursday, Conservative MP and former minister Dame Priti Patel said: "Andy Burnham's obsession with the EU risks dragging Britain backwards, damaging our economy and leaving hardworking British taxpayers footing the bill." The Liberal Democrats earlier this month described the draft deal as a "patch, not a fix" and said the "real solution is to re-join the single market and to establish a customs union with the EU". Reform UK believes one of the "key benefits" of Brexit is that Britain no longer has to "adhere to ridiculous EU rules" and any form of alignment could have a negative impact on the country's trade policy. The Green Party has called for the UK to re-join the customs union, with leader Zack Polanski previously saying "full membership of the EU remains the best option for the UK". events.title: ‘Bring Back THE Boss’: Nvidia Employees Petition for Jensen Huang’s Return
events.summary: Some Nvidia employees are calling for Jensen Huang’s return even after his multiple reported extramarital affairs and abrupt resignation , according to internal correspondence reviewed by WIRED. An internal “suggestion box” post submitted before Huang’s resignation by a longtime engineer at Nvidia urged the company’s board to take employee sentiment into consideration prior to taking any action. The submission has attracted more than 1,600 comments since then, with several asking board members to find a way to bring back Huang. “If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” wrote one anonymous commenter. “We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance,” wrote another. One employee went as far as sending a companywide email demanding transparency into Huang’s exit. “I stand by Jensen,” the staffer wrote. “Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us.” The employee couldn’t be reached for comment, while the engineer behind the suggestion box post declined to comment. Nvidia and its new board chair, investor Harvey Jones, didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. Huang, a 63-year-old who had led Nvidia since its founding in 1993, wrote in an email to employees on Sunday that he had been “unfaithful to [his] wife” and that there was “no excuse.” The acknowledgement followed reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset . The board announced Huang’s resignation on Thursday morning, following reports of an alleged second affair with a direct report. (This employee has not commented on the matter.) Since then, Reuters reported on an alleged affair with yet another Nvidia employee. Huang hasn’t commented about these reports since his Sunday email. Nvidia’s board is largely made up of early Nvidia investors and Huang’s longtime confidants. It named Nvidia chief financial officer Colette Kress interim CEO and appointed former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones as chair of the board. The crisis has cost the company $1 trillion in market value since the allegations surfaced, prompted investigations from US lawmakers and the FBI, and raised the prospect of new export controls on chips. It’s been business as usual inside the company throughout this week, but Huang’s resignation left many employees stunned . In the hours after, about two dozen employees posted on LinkedIn in support of Huang, with one describing their faith in his leadership as unwavering. Over the same period, WIRED couldn’t identify any posts from Nvidia employees in support of his resignation. One employee who has been at Nvidia for a couple of years and wasn’t authorized to speak publicly says they perceive the desire for Huang’s reinstatement as widespread. They worry the company will eventually suffer without its founder at the helm and say that the board must bring him back. “Nvidia is Nvidia because of Jensen,” the employee tells WIRED. Many employees had expected a board investigation to conclude before any big changes would occur. For instance, the suggestion-box post called on the board to share its findings with employees and formally solicit their sentiment “about Jensen’s continuing as our CEO.” Instead, Huang left just as the inquiry had begun. Staffers are seeking to better understand why. “If America fails the man who helped build its future,” the employee in the companywide email stated, “then this world does not deserve Jensen Huang.” In your inbox: Inside WIRED’s newsroom with Katie Drummond They war-gamed dimming the sun —it went worse than you think The Big Interview: Nathan Fielder tells us everything Live tracker: Elon Musk’s America PAC is spending big on the midterms Introducing the app: More ways to make the most of WIRED © 2026 Condé Nast. events.title: ‘Renewed confidence’: Singtel lifts FY2027 guidance as underlying profit grows 10%, net profit falls 55%
events.summary: Singtel’s revision came on the back of an 8.7% rise in first-half operating companies’ earnings before interest and taxes to $902 million. Singtel’s H1 net profit fell 55% to S$1.54 billion after last year’s S$2.21 billion divestment gains were not repeated. Underlying net profit rose 10% to S$1.49 billion, helped by NCS, Digital InfraCo, Optus, Airtel and AIS. Revenue rose 6% to S$7.29 billion. Singtel lifted its interim dividend to S$0.09 and raised full-year OpCo Ebit guidance. SINGAPORE – Telecommunications giant Singtel on Nov 13 raised financial year 2027 growth guidance for its operating companies’ (Opco) earnings before interest and taxes (Ebit) to between mid and high single digits. This was an upgrade from the guidance of low- to mid-single-digit growth it gave in May , and the second year in a row that the telco has raised its Opco Ebit guidance at the half-year mark. The revision came on the back of an 8.7% rise in first-half Opco Ebit to $902 million. The growth was led by strong performance by Australian subsidiary Optus, tech service provider NCS and its digital infrastructure arm Digital InfraCo. Optus’ Ebit rose 13.7% to A$322 million (S$282 million), NCS’ rose 15.5% to $212 million and Digital InfraCo’s rose 25.3% to $51 million. Arthur Lang, group chief financial officer of Singtel, said at a media briefing of the company’s first-half results on Nov 13 that the telco was entering the second half of the year “with a renewed confidence versus six months ago”. His comments came even as the telco reported a 54.7% drop in net profit to $1.5 billion for the first half ended September, in the absence of exceptional gains recorded the previous year. Underlying profit for the period was up 10.4% at $1.5 billion. Lang said that when the group set its initial set of guidance in May, the Strait of Hormuz crisis had just broken out and inflation was a concern. Moreover, the proposed merger of Simba and M1 had just been called off, adding a new degree of uncertainty. In addition, Singtel said that it was also reviewing its capital expenditure guidance of about $3 billion. The group expects capital expenditure to be lower than initially estimated on the back of disciplined capital allocation. However, Singtel Singapore’s Ebit was down 4.5% as a result of the absence of one-off income recorded in the corresponding period the previous year. Excluding the one-off, Singtel Singapore’s Ebit was down 1%. Singapore mobile service revenue grew 3.8% in the second quarter from the first quarter , its second consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Group chief executive Yuen Kuan Moon said this followed seven quarters of decline. Average revenue per user rose to $23 for the quarter ended Sept 30, from $22 the previous quarter. The telco attributed the rise to its three-brand strategy of Singtel, Gomo and hi!. “We are not interested in going after just the pure volume of subscribers,” said Ng Tian Chong, CEO of Singtel Singapore. Optus stake sale still on the table In July , Singtel confirmed that it was in discussion with interested parties to sell a stake in Optus. Yuen said Singtel’s search for a minority “like-minded Australian partner” for Optus was still ongoing. However, given the strong performance of Optus, Lang noted that a stake in the company will not be available “at any value”. Earlier media reports noted that New Zealand-based infrastructure investor Morrison was in talks to buy a minority stake valued at more than A$2 billion. Singtel said that its first-half financial year 2027 net profit decline was mainly due to the absence of $2.2 billion in net exceptional gains recorded a year earlier from the partial sale of its stake in Airtel and the Intouch-Gulf Energy merger. Excluding exceptional items, underlying net profit rose about 10% from $1.4 billion a year earlier. The group’s operating revenue rose 5.5% to $7.3 billion in the first half , from $6.9 billion in the year-ago period. In constant currency terms, revenue would have increased 1.4%, while underlying net profit would have grown 15.9%, Singtel said. The board approved an interim dividend of nine cents per share, comprising a core dividend of 7.1 cents and a value realisation dividend of 1.9 cents . This was 10% higher than the 8.2 cents per share declared a year earlier.

events.title: Applied Materials forecasts quarterly revenue above estimates on strong AI chip demand
events.summary: Applied Materials is benefiting from increased spending by chipmakers racing to meet the extraordinary AI-led demand for chips and memory. Applied Materials expects fiscal first-quarter revenue of about US$11.10 billion, above Wall Street’s US$10.89 billion estimate, as AI chip demand keeps spending high. Fourth-quarter Semiconductor Systems revenue rose 64% to US$8 billion, and adjusted profit was US$4.16 a share, beating forecasts. Chief executive Gary Dickerson said 2027 could be “another record year”, with wafer fab equipment demand set to rise more than 30% and customers wanting tools sooner. Applied Materials forecast fiscal first-quarter revenue above Wall Street expectations on Nov 12 , betting that strong demand for advanced AI chips will continue to fuel spending on its semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The company, which supplies equipment for key wafer fabrication processes, is benefiting from increased spending by chipmakers racing to meet the extraordinary artificial intelligence-led demand for chips and memory. “The actual metrics of the market show that demand is still very strong,” said Bob O’Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research. Applied’s results show chipmakers and foundries are “buying as much equipment as they possibly can”, he added. The Santa Clara, California-based company’s Semiconductor Systems revenue jumped to US$8 billion (S$10.3 billion) in the fourth quarter, up about 64% from a year earlier. The company is one of Apple’s partners for its American Manufacturing Program, which includes work at Applied’s Austin, Texas, facility to boost US production of chipmaking equipment. “We expect 2027 to be another record year for the market and Applied,” chief executive Gary Dickerson said on a post-earnings call. He said wafer fab equipment demand should rise more than 30% and customers are asking for tools sooner, not later. China accounted for 25% of fourth-quarter revenue, down from 29% a year earlier, though sales there rose about 35% to US$2.64 billion. The company forecast quarterly revenue of around US$11.1 billion, plus or minus US$500 million, compared with the average of analysts’ estimates of US$10.89 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. The company reported fourth-quarter adjusted profit of US$4.16 per share, beating analysts’ average estimate of US$4.05. REUTERS
